title: How Much Does Exterior Trim Installation Cost? [2026 Data] | Angi
summary: Discover the cost to install exterior trim. Learn about price factors, labor, materials, and ways to save on your exterior trim installation project.
body_markdown:
Written by[Mitchell Grant](https://www.angi.com/articles/author/mitchell-grant) Contributing Writer Reviewed by[Morgan Rousseau](https://www.angi.com/articles/author/morgan-rousseau) Editor Updated Sep 17, 2026 [Add to Preferred Sources (opens in a new tab)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=angi.com) Cost Insights: - Professional exterior trim installation ranges from **$500** to **$9,000** , with most homeowners paying around **$1,800** for your complete project. - Your trim material choice and your home's architectural details determine the complexity and labor hours needed for proper installation. - Budget for permits ranging from $50 to $300, plus disposal fees and painting or staining to finish your new exterior trim. - [Hiring a local siding professional](https://www.angi.com/nearme/siding-contractors/) prevents water damage and ensures your trim withstands harsh weather for years. In 2026, the national average cost to install exterior trim is **$1,800** . Most homeowners spend between **$1,000** and **$4,500** , or roughly **$6** **to $15 per linear foot** , depending on trim material and project size. Larger homes or custom trim profiles can push costs toward the higher end of that range. ## **Exterior Trim Cost by Size: Project Scope and Footage** The size and scope of your exterior trim project are the primary drivers of total cost, since every additional linear foot adds to both material and labor expenses. Smaller homes cover the basic perimeter plus a few windows and doors, while larger or multi-story homes require significantly more footage. Complex architectural features like bay windows, dormers, or wraparound porches increase the amount of trim needed even further. Here is a breakdown of typical costs by project scope: Home Size/Project Scope Lin. Ft. of Trim Average Cost in 2026 Small home/partial facade 100–150 $600–$2,250 Medium home/full trim 200–300 $1,200–$4,500 Large home/complex features 400–600 $2,400–$9,000 The number of windows, doors, and corners on your home also directly affects the amount of trim you'll need. Choosing to install trim on the entire exterior versus just a section—like a front façade—will also change your project's price. ## **Exterior Trim Material Costs: How Type Affects Budget** The type of exterior trim you choose directly shapes your project's cost, appearance, and long-term durability. Common options include fascia boards, soffits (which are the least costly), window and door casings, corner boards, and decorative moldings (which are the most costly), each serving a distinct purpose and carrying its own installation complexity. Standard profiles are the most budget-friendly choice, while custom millwork and ornate details increase both material and labor costs. The following table shows per-linear-foot cost ranges by trim type: Trim Type Cost per Lin. Ft. in 2026 Pros Cons Fascia $6–$12 Essential for gutters, clean look Prone to water damage if wood Soffit $4–$10 Ventilation, protects rafters Can be hard to access Window/door casing $5–$15 Boosts curb appeal, seals gaps Custom shapes cost more Corner boards $6–$14 Protects corners, accent detail May require custom fitting Decorative molding $10–$25 Unique look, boosts value Higher labor, upkeep ## **Exterior Trim Costs by Location: Where Labor Varies Most** Where you live has a meaningful impact on exterior trim installation costs, driven by differences in local labor rates, material availability, and building codes. Urban areas consistently carry higher labor costs than rural locations. Homes in wet or coastal climates may also require premium, weather-resistant materials that add to the overall budget. Some cities and regions require permits for exterior trim work, which can further affect your total cost. ## **Exterior Trim Cost Factors: What Determines the Price?** Several factors influence the cost to install exterior trim. Understanding these can help you plan and budget effectively. ### **Labor** Labor for exterior trim installation runs **$40 to $90 per hour** , with rates varying based on the professional's specialty and your project's complexity. Skilled carpenters, general contractors, and siding specialists all handle this work, and charges may be structured by the hour, per linear foot, or as a flat project rate. Minimum service fees apply to small jobs, making them relatively more expensive per foot, and costs rise further for multi-story homes or hard-to-reach areas. Labor includes preparation, installation, caulking, and cleanup, but always confirm with your contractor. ### **Permits** [Permit costs](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-building-permit-cost.htm) for exterior trim installation range from **$50 to $300** , depending on your location and whether your home falls under strict building codes or historic district rules. Your contractor often handles the permit application, but clarify that responsibility before work begins. Permit requirements can affect both your project timeline and your budget, so factor them into your planning early. ### **Additional Features** Decorative moldings, crown details, and custom millwork add style and value to your exterior trim but also increase both material and labor costs. Weatherproofing upgrades—such as flashing, premium caulking, or advanced sealants—protect your home from the elements while adding to your materials bill. [Painting or staining the trim](https://www.angi.com/articles/best-exterior-and-interior-trim.htm) after installation is another expense to plan for, and some homeowners also choose insulated trim or trim integrated with gutters or siding for added energy efficiency and protection. ### **Installation Add-Ons** There are several factors that influence total labor costs when installing exterior trim: - **Intricate profiles** , curved or angled trim, and multi-story work increase complexity and cost. - **Accessibility challenges** , such as steep roofs or dense landscaping, may require scaffolding or extra labor. - **Site preparation** , including removing old trim, disposal fees, and delivery of new materials, can add to your budget. - [Post-construction cleanup](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-it-cost-clean-construction-site.htm) and debris removal are sometimes charged separately. - **Design or architectural consultation fees** may apply for custom projects. - **Inspections** could be required by local codes or homeowner's associations. ## **Exterior Trim Additional Costs: What to Budget For** Beyond installation, there are ongoing and one-time costs to keep in mind for your exterior trim project. ### **Warranties** Exterior trim often comes with manufacturer or installer warranties covering defects or premature failure for five to 25 years. Extended warranties and service plans are sometimes available for an additional fee. Warranties can meaningfully reduce long-term repair and replacement expenses, but always review the fine print for coverage limits and exclusions before committing. ### **Maintenance** Annual exterior trim maintenance costs range from **$50 to $300** , depending on your home's size and the material you chose. Wood trim demands the most upkeep, requiring more frequent painting and caulking, while PVC, fiber cement, and aluminum are significantly lower-maintenance. Watch for early warning signs like peeling paint or soft spots so you can address problems before they become costly repairs. ### **Taxes** Sales tax on materials and labor varies by state and can add to your project total. If your trim installation is part of a major remodel, your property taxes could increase slightly due to a higher home value. ### **Insurance** Homeowner's insurance may cover exterior trim damage caused by storms or accidents, but it does not cover routine wear or neglect. Installing new trim does not increase your insurance premiums, though it is always worth reviewing your policy to confirm your coverage. Any contractor you hire should carry liability and workers' compensation insurance to protect you from financial risk during the project. ## **How Much Does an Exterior Trim Pro Cost?** A[local exterior trim pro](https://www.angi.com/nearme/siding-contractors/) charges **$40 to $90 per hour** in labor, making professional installation accessible for most budgets. Hiring a pro is the smartest choice to avoid installation errors and unexpected expenses. ### **Here's why it's ideal to hire an exterior trim installation pro** When you hire a pro, you're not only paying for the hours they work on your project, but the years they spent mastering their craft. Some other reasons to hire a pro are: - Pros understand trim materials, especially wood, better than homeowners. - Trim undergoes a beating, and professionals know how to install it in order to withstand the elements. - A proper installation prevents costly water damage to the home. - If you are only doing a part of your home, a pro can match the new section to the old section. - Having a second set of eyes on the integrity of your home is never a bad idea. - Professionals will be familiar with the building codes and requirements for your area. - If using wood, pros can arrange it to appear more cohesive by matching the wood's grain direction. ### **If you want to DIY an exterior trim installation** There are some steps you can take to get the project set up for a pro (which we recommend). You can help by: - Taking quality photos of the exterior of the entire home. - Clear any landscaping or bushes that are in the way. Trim and tree limbs close to the house. - If your pro gives the go-ahead, you can remove some existing pieces yourself. - Inform your pro about any damage you may have noticed in the past, even if it was years ago. - If you have an HOA, ensure that your new exterior trim adheres to their guidelines. - Remove any window boxes, wasp nests, or other signs of animal life. ## **Exterior Trim Replacement vs. Repair** Repairs to exterior trim run **$100 to $500** , making them the right call for minor issues like small cracks, loose sections, or isolated rot. Full replacement is recommended when there is widespread rot, water damage, or trim that no longer matches your home's style. A good rule of thumb: if the cost to repair exceeds 50% of[trim replacement costs](https://www.angi.com/articles/cost-to-repair-replace-trim.htm) , replacement is the better long-term investment. Assess the age and warranty status of your trim to help make your decision. ## **Does Exterior Trim Add Value to Your Home?** Installing new exterior trim offers a strong return on investment (ROI), often recouping **60% to 80%** of its cost at resale. Fresh trim enhances curb appeal, making your home more attractive to buyers and improving first impressions. Compared to other exterior projects like siding or windows, trim is a relatively affordable upgrade with noticeable results. The quality of materials, design, color choice, and installation craftsmanship all influence your ROI. Besides value, new trim can improve weather resistance, energy efficiency, and overall safety while boosting your home’s visual character. ## **Tips to Reduce Costs While Installing Exterior Trim** Here are some helpful tips to keep exterior trim installation costs within budget: - Get multiple quotes from licensed, insured contractors. - Choose budget-friendly materials that offer durability and low maintenance. - Limit custom profiles or ornate designs to reduce labor and material costs. - Schedule installation during off-peak seasons for potential discounts. - DIY prep or removal of old trim if safe and feasible. - Bundle exterior trim installation with other exterior projects (e.g., siding, painting) for package pricing. - Maintain trim regularly to avoid costly repairs or premature replacement. Next Steps: Finalize Your Project With a Pro - Check to make sure your pro is recycling the material if it’s a requirement in your area. - If you have wood trim, you may be able to repurpose it for other projects if it’s in good condition. - Make sure disposal fees are marked in the quote. - As you should for most professionals, verify that their insurance and licenses are current.
